evidence.testTitle: [USER-001 USER-002 USER-003 USER-004 USER-005 USER-006 USER-012 USER-013 USER-014] independent profile fields bind paths queries and bodies to the authenticated actor
evidence.scenarioScope: Selected profile fields and current/legacy paths; structured profile event feature is not claimed.
evidence.rationale: Real independent account credentials, public REST and IRC entrypoints, live recipient controls and a recreated Workerd/SQLite runtime.
assertionDetails: Authorized own displayName, avatar and customStatus are canonicalized and delivered to a subscribed shared-channel peer and second own device; an outsider without a shared channel does not receive them.
Current and legacy foreign profile paths and IRC METADATA target writes are denied for each field; an independently bounded event/IRC observer window is silent except for live barriers.

Separately, username query and body substitutions for each field apply only to Alice; ignored identity and privileged fields do not give Alice roles or admin access, Bob and Charlie profiles are unchanged, and fresh logins/readback survive runtime recreation.
After recreation, each foreign field write is repeated against both actual profile aliases and independent Bob and Charlie profiles remain unchanged.

Each canonical field and every query/body substitution is observed with exact 761 recipient, Alice or AliceAlt target nickname, key and value; PING-bounded recipient slices reject any other target for the same key/value.

evidence.testTitle: [USER-007 USER-009] foreign password resets fail and persisted password and SCRAM secrets stay out of responses and streams
evidence.scenarioScope: Cross-user admin reset, actual stored credential filtering and live recipient observations; no unsupported self-reset endpoint claimed.
evidence.rationale: Real independent account credentials, public REST and IRC entrypoints, live recipient controls and a recreated Workerd/SQLite runtime.
assertionDetails: Alice receives 403 on both actual admin password-reset prefixes targeting Bob, while authorized administrator resets an independent account and its new credentials work.

Actual Bob password hash, SCRAM salt and stored/server keys were read from SQLite and compared in memory against requester/admin response bodies and live IRC/event streams without logging secret values; Bob hash and SCRAM record remain byte-for-byte unchanged.

After runtime recreation fresh Bob, Alice and reset-account logins retain correct identities; Alice is again denied a Bob password reset and the cross-user profile response excludes the actual stored secrets.

evidence.testTitle: [USER-010 USER-011] NickServ grouping registration and drop retain exact nickname owners after recreation
evidence.scenarioScope: Actual NickServ GROUP, SAREGISTER and DROP semantics; GROUP ignores target arguments and groups the current nickname.
evidence.rationale: Real independent account credentials, public REST and IRC entrypoints, live recipient controls and a recreated Workerd/SQLite runtime.
assertionDetails: Bob groups his own BobExtra and Alice groups and drops her own AliceExtra as positive controls. Bob cannot assume Alice nickname, NS GROUP alice still groups BobExtra, SAREGISTER alice is denied and DROP alice is denied.

IRC and event observers receive positive barriers without outputs from the attempted foreign operations; exact Alice, Bob, BobExtra and unrelated Charlie nickname owners are independently read from SQLite.
After recreation fresh independent logins retain IDs, Bob repeats NICK, GROUP, SAREGISTER and DROP attempts, and exact nickname owners remain unchanged.

AliceExtra GROUP is independently read as Alice-owned before and after recreation; the actual owner DROP is independently read as absent before and after another recreation while BobExtra and primary nicknames retain their owners.
